text: Market Activities – Phase 3 (EOP-F) Stakeholder Engagement and Market Analysis: Element 16 secured a signed agreement with Searles Valley Minerals, a mining and mineral processing company in the Mojave Desert, to host a pilot project integrating sulfur thermal energy storage for industrial process heat at their facility. While Searles Valley Minerals is contributing cost share, the project is largely funded by a grant from the California Energy Commission (CEC). The core objective of the project is to demonstrate the reliable and flexible operation of sulfur TES technology in providing dispatchable process heat and reducing fossil fuel consumption in on-site industrial boilers. In order to investigate and understand the detailed, practical considerations at industrial facilities, Element 16 conducted site visits and held in-person meetings with the following companies: a) Searles Valley Minerals, a 150-year-old mining company. These visits led to Element 16’s new grant funded project to deploy sulfur thermal energy storage charged by grid electricity at their plant in Trona, CA. b) Petroleum Development Oman, a national oil company that owns and operates the Miraah Solar Field in Oman, which was built by California-based GlassPoint Solar. This is one of the world’s largest solar thermal installations for process heat around 300 Celsius. Page 63 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. c) Abu Dhabi National Oil Corporation (ADNOC) is not only an operator of a large sour gas plant with heavy steam usage but also operates the world’s largest sulfur production plant. d) A Nordic energy company that provides electricity and heat to industrial facilities, including mining and pulp/paper mills. e) Three concentrated solar steam companies that provide (or aim to provide) renewable steam for industrial steam users. Technology/Knowledge Transfer Activities Project progress and technical developments were disseminated widely to stakeholders, customers, and key decision makers. Some notable public events where Element 16 team presented as a panelist, and/or presented as a speaker, on sulfur thermal energy storage technology include: Cleantech and Energy Storage a. RE+ in Irvine, CA and Las Vegas, NV. Element 16 has spoken on stage at the last two RE+ events, as a guest of the US Department of Energy’s Solar Energy Technology Office. At these events, Element 16 presented progress to a broad audience including government agency stakeholders, investors, and other cleantech innovators. b. SolarPACES in Rome, Italy. Element 16 presented sulfur thermal energy storage for industrial process heat to leading academic and industry solar experts at SolarPACES. This presentation to a highly technical audience was very well received and has led to collaboration opportunities in Europe. c. SET Tech and Urban Innovation Forum. As part of a US Delegation to Germany, Element 16 spoke at two cleantech-focused events in Berlin, Germany. Element 16 was able to meet with multiple cleantech venture capitalists through these events. d. Northeast Clean Energy Counsel’s Navigate event. Element 16 was selected for this exclusive event in Boston, Massachusetts, where Element 16 met with some of the largest industrial corporate energy venture investors one-on-one, including Bosch, Equinor, and PTT Chemical.
